title: Lighter daily sins tolerated in the regenerate without loss of heaven
source_text: VII. Porro ex hac peccatorum inter se disparitate & inaequalitate, & aliorum prae aliis levitate, sive gravitate, fit ut Deus cum filiis suis, quos adoptavit in Christo, & Spiritu suo regeneravit, juxta gratiosum foedus Evangelii benigne agens, peccata quaedam leviora in iis eatenus toleret, ut etiamsi non sint sine ejusmodi peccatis, in quae quotidie incurrunt, & in aliquo eorum moriantur, non tamen eos propterea declaret indignos qui in coelum admittantur, & gloriae ac felicitatis aeternae participes fiant. Adeoque peccata talia consistere possunt cum bona conscientia, & munditia cordis, eaque mensura sanctificationis, quam Deus a nobis exigit in hac vita, ut in altera ipso frui, ipsumque videre possimus. Neque ejusmodi peccata ex homine fideli & pio excutiunt conscientiae pacem, & gaudium spiritus, ac remissionis peccatorum ipsius, & salutis aeternae spem atque fiduciam. Cujus generis peccata sunt, exempli gratia, verbum otiosum, risus immoderatus, cogitatio vana, & naevi ac defectus omnes adhaerentes bonorum piorum operibus, in quibus a summa legis exactitudine semper deficiunt.
pass_a_gloss: Further, from this disparity and inequality of sins among themselves, and the lightness or gravity of some beyond others, it comes about that God, dealing kindly with his sons whom he adopted in Christ and regenerated by his Spirit, according to the gracious covenant of the Gospel, so far tolerates certain lighter sins in them that even if they are not without sins of that sort into which they daily fall, and die in some one of them, he nevertheless does not on that account declare them unworthy to be admitted into heaven and made partakers of eternal glory and happiness. And so such sins can stand with a good conscience and purity of heart and that measure of sanctification which God requires of us in this life that in the next we may enjoy him and see him. Nor do sins of that kind shake out of a faithful and godly man the peace of conscience and joy of spirit and the hope and confidence of the remission of his sins and of eternal salvation. Of which kind are, for example, an idle word, immoderate laughter, a vain thought, and all the blemishes and defects clinging to the good works of the godly, in which they always fall short of the utmost exactness of the law.
pass_b_english: Under the gospel covenant God bears the regenerate’s lighter daily faults without barring heaven.
Idle words, vain thoughts, and flaws in good works can coexist with peace of conscience and hope of salvation.

choices.why: Paternal forbearance, not indifference to sin.
